chunks: 5. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Haytham al-Ijli; Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qittan; Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani; al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mukattab; Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Sa'igh, and Ali ibn Abd Allah al-Warraq (may Allah be pleased with them) said: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyyah al-Qittan said: Bakr ibn Abd Allah ibn Habib said: Tamim ibn Buhlul said: Abu Mu'awiyah said, from al-A'mash, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them):

He said regarding what was described to him of the laws of religion: Verily, Allah does not impose on a soul except its capacity, nor does He burden it beyond its power. The actions of the servants are created with created [taqdir] creation, not with constitutive [takwin] creation, and Allah is the Creator of all things. We do not say with determinism (jabr), nor with relinquishment (tafwid). And Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, does not take the innocent for the guilty, nor does Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, punish children for the sins of their fathers, for He said in the clear part of His Book: 'And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another' and He said, the Mighty and Exalted: 'And that man shall have nothing but what he strives for.' And to Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, belongs the power to pardon and bestow favor, and it is not befitting for Him, the Mighty and Exalted, to oppress. Nor does Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, impose on His servants the obedience of one He knows will mislead them and lead them astray. Nor does He choose for His message or select from His servants one He knows will disbelieve in Him and worship Satan instead of Him. Nor does He appoint over His creation a proof except an infallible one. The hadith is long; we have taken from it the place of need, and I have included it in its entirety in the book Al-Khasa'il.
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia theological view on divine decree and human free will regarding the creation of actions?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) articulates the distinct Shia doctrine of 'Amr bayn al-Amrayn' (the position between the two extremes), distinguishing between God's creative act (takwin) and His decree (taqdir) to affirm human free will without denying divine omnipotence. It emphasizes that God’s justice precludes punishing the innocent or burdening souls beyond their capacity, ensuring that His chosen prophets and imams are infallible (ma'sum) to serve as perfect guides. This theological framework underpins the Shia understanding of divine justice (Adl) and the necessity of infallible leadership for correct religious guidance.
